image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a black assault rifle (resembling an AR-15/M4 platform) against a white background. Visible components include the upper receiver with a Picatinny rail and flip-up sights, a handguard with M-LOK slots, a pistol grip, a trigger guard, a detachable box magazine, and a portion of the lower receiver. The image appears to be a digital rendering or AI generation due to slight texture uniformity and edge artifacts.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Surfaces lack realistic micro-scratches, wear patterns, or machining marks. The texture is overly smooth and uniform, resembling a low-poly 3D render rather than a photograph of a used firearm.
The bottom of the magazine appears to melt or blend into the white background without a distinct edge or shadow, suggesting a segmentation or generation error.
The geometry of the rear sight block looks slightly warped; the hinge mechanism lacks clear definition and seems to fuse with the rail.
There are faint, nonsensical engravings/markings on the left side of the upper receiver (near the red dot). They resemble text or serial numbers but are illegible gibberish, a common AI artifact.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific model variant (e.g., M4 vs AK) and ensure it aligns with the 'assault rifle' class label despite the cropping.
To verify the physical separation between the magazine and the receiver, and to check for edge bleeding into the white background.
To assess the realism of the metal/polymer textures and identify subtle rendering artifacts like the gibberish text.
To ensure the flip-up sights and rail slots have correct 3D depth and are not flattened or distorted.

focus_areas: Integrity of the magazine well connection
Realism of surface textures (metal vs polymer)
Clarity of mechanical details (sights, trigger group)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'gibberish markings' artifact. AI often fails to replicate real firearm serial numbers or safety selectors accurately, resulting in nonsensical shapes. Also, verify if the lack of a stock is a framing choice or a generation failure (inpainting issue).
